program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding deep passes; consolidate and run heavy validation after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Direct PubMed/NCBI discovery and abstract verification
PMID-level dedupe against cumulative Wave 2000 index and rolling deep-state

waves.focus: Meta-analysis of 12 RCTs found preoperative nebulized magnesium sulfate substantially reduced postoperative sore throat through 24 hours without increasing hemodynamic risk, while hoarseness and cough were not significantly reduced; evidence is for a perioperative nebulized route, not oral magnesium.

Meta-analysis of 25 RCTs reported improved ventricular remodeling, inflammatory markers, natriuretic peptides, and clinical effectiveness with standardized Rhodiola rosea injection in HFrEF without more adverse reactions; methodological shortcomings and the injectable standardized-drug formulation prevent generalization to oral Rhodiola supplements.

Meta-analysis of observational studies found no statistically significant association between dietary choline or betaine intake and incident type 2 diabetes; certainty was very low and heterogeneity was substantial.

Meta-analysis of 11 randomized crossover studies found caffeine plus carbohydrate improved high-intensity interval exercise performance versus placebo or carbohydrate controls, but not versus caffeine alone; publication bias was detected and overall certainty was low, suggesting caffeine may account for much of the effect.

Network meta-analysis in CKD found possible intervention-specific advantages for cholecalciferol, sodium bicarbonate, and protein supplementation, but no significant differences among interventions for several muscle and metabolic outcomes; small heterogeneous studies limit comparative conclusions.

Meta-analysis of 12 RCTs found no overall reduction in childhood asthma or wheeze with early-life omega-3 supplementation; benefit appeared only in high-dose and high-EPA subgroups, so dose-response findings remain subgroup evidence rather than dosing guidance.

Twelve-week RCT in 192 women with PCOS/PMOS found metformin, inositol, diet, and combined therapy all improved metabolic or endocrine outcomes, with the multimodal combination producing the largest changes; the design does not isolate the combination benefit to inositol.

Meta-analysis across microbiota-modulating exposures in cancer immunotherapy associated probiotic use with better response and survival, while antibiotics were associated with worse outcomes and FMT showed favorable response rates; heterogeneous intervention classes and likely observational evidence prevent a standalone probiotic efficacy claim.

Systematic review of four studies found topical or systemic capsaicin was associated with lower burning-mouth pain scores, but study risk of bias was moderate to critical and overall certainty was low or very low.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found vitamin C-based gingival depigmentation showed short-term improvement at one month, but no significant difference at three months and high heterogeneity; protocols and adjunctive approaches varied.

Meta-analysis of 22 pregnancy trials found daily iron-folate produced slightly higher hemoglobin overall, while intermittent regimens caused fewer gastrointestinal adverse effects and had better adherence; anemia incidence did not clearly differ.
Meta-analysis of 12 RCTs found vitamin D supplementation did not improve lung function, asthma control scores, FeNO, or IgE in children with asthma; this is a direct condition-specific null finding.

Meta-analysis of 8 RCTs reported better liver-function and inflammatory outcomes when Chinese herbal medicine was added to Western medicine for icteric hepatitis, with no significant adverse-event difference; high risk of bias, heterogeneity, and multi-herb treatment prevent ingredient-level attribution.

Meta-analysis of 27 RCTs reported better response, NIHSS, and Barthel outcomes when injectable ginkgo terpene lactone preparations were added to antiplatelet therapy for ischemic stroke, without more adverse events; combination therapy and injectable formulations prevent generalization to oral ginkgo.

Meta-analysis of 9 RCTs found perioperative magnesium sulfate infusion reduced postoperative pain scores and opioid consumption after spinal or neurologic surgery without major adverse events; evidence is route- and procedure-specific.

Meta-analysis of 19 RCTs found Rhodiola crenulata extract was not clearly superior to Western medicine for oxygenation but outperformed placebo on oxygenation and clinical symptoms in acute high-altitude disease; evidence is population- and extract-specific with low-certainty concerns.

Meta-analysis of 10 RCTs found no broad lipid superiority for Ginkgo biloba extract versus proprietary Chinese or Western medicines; isolated HDL, age, and dose subgroup signals were heterogeneous and should not be converted into dosing guidance.

Systematic review/meta-analysis of five RCTs in 66 female volleyball players found no clear ergogenic benefit of acute caffeine for sport-specific, physical, or physiological performance outcomes; hand tremor, anxiety, and excessive stimulation were reported and certainty was very low.

Bayesian network meta-analysis of 36 RCTs found whey ranked highest for lean-mass gains when combined with resistance training, but dose-response and age subgroup estimates were exploratory and certainty for comparisons was low to very low.

Meta-analysis of 35 RCTs involving 114,592 participants found increased atrial-fibrillation risk only among high-cardiovascular-risk participants receiving more than 1,500 mg/day EPA/DHA, with no significant risk increase in the other dose/risk strata; this supports a dose- and risk-context safety signal rather than a universal omega-3 warning.

Randomized trial found cinnamon leaf-oil inhalation, alone or with higher oxygen concentration, did not reduce nausea or vomiting during the first six hours after cesarean section under spinal anesthesia; evidence is aromatherapy-route specific.

Meta-analysis of randomized trials in healthy people found probiotic supplementation did not significantly change fecal butyrate, acetate, or propionate concentrations; this is a direct mechanistic null in healthy populations.

Systematic review of 24 cancer-supportive-care studies found heterogeneous ginger results across nausea/vomiting, xerostomia, nutrition, fatigue, and quality of life, including some studies reporting no benefit or disadvantage; formulations and endpoints varied widely.

Meta-analysis found no significant short-term efficacy difference between microneedling with vitamin C and microneedling with tranexamic acid for melasma; both appeared tolerable, but long-term safety and recurrence were not established and evidence is procedure/route-specific.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found probiotics/prebiotics had little or no effect on hemoglobin, with small ferritin and fractional-iron-absorption signals in women of reproductive age and no clear benefit in children; certainty ranged from moderate to very low and effects were strain/product dependent.
